episode_title: 今日雙語精華：放克音樂、虎鯨悲歌與北韓駭客
episode_summary: 哈囉，各位聽眾！今天是二零二六年十一月十三日，歡迎收聽每日五分鐘雙語精華。今天我們將聊聊經典歌曲《Play That Funky Music》的爆笑創作故事、圈養虎鯨令人心疼的牙齒問題，以及北韓駭客如何利用假視訊電話詐騙四億美元加密貨幣。精彩內容，不容錯過！

selected_links.title: TIL the song Play That Funky Music by Wild Cherry came about when they were playing for a mostly Black crowd and during a break a patron asked "Are you going to play some funky music, white boys?" so they wrote up the song in 5 minutes.
TIL captive orcas frequently have worn-down, broken, or intentionally drilled teeth because they chew and grind on concrete pool walls and steel gates out of stress and boredom
North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI

segments.zh: 哈囉各位聽眾，歡迎收聽二零二六年十一月十三日的每日五分鐘雙語精華。
segments.en: Hey everyone, welcome to today's five-minute bilingual highlights on November thirteenth, two thousand twenty-six.

segments.zh: 我是你們的主持人，今天我們要深入探討三個超有趣又發人深省的話題。
segments.en: I'm your host, and today we're diving into three super interesting and thought-provoking topics.

segments.zh: 從一首經典放克歌曲的爆笑由來，到令人心疼的動物福利議題，還有最新的網路詐騙手法。
segments.en: From the hilarious origin of a classic funk song to a heartbreaking animal welfare issue and the latest online scam tactics.

segments.zh: 首先，我們來聊聊一首大家耳熟能詳的經典歌曲《Play That Funky Music》。
segments.en: First up, let's talk about a classic song everyone knows: "Play That Funky Music."

segments.zh: 你知道嗎？這首歌的誕生，竟然是一次超級即興的意外！
segments.en: Did you know this song was born from a totally spontaneous and unexpected moment?

segments.zh: 樂團Wild Cherry當時在一個幾乎都是黑人觀眾的場合表演。
segments.en: The band Wild Cherry was performing for a crowd that was mostly Black at the time.

segments.zh: 休息時，一位觀眾問：「白人小子，你們會不會玩點放克音樂啊？」
segments.en: During a break, a patron asked, "Are you going to play some funky music, white boys?"

segments.zh: 結果，他們就在五分鐘內寫出了這首傳奇金曲！
segments.en: And just like that, they wrote this legendary hit song in only five minutes!

segments.zh: Reddit網友們都笑翻了，說這根本是史上最棒的歌曲創作故事。
segments.en: Redditors cracked up, saying it's simply the best song origin story ever.

segments.zh: 有人說：「這就是真正的觀眾參與啊！」
segments.en: One user commented, "Now that's what I call true audience participation!"

segments.zh: 還有網友開玩笑說：「想像他們如果拒絕了會怎樣？」
segments.en: Another Redditor joked, "Imagine what would've happened if they had said no?"

segments.zh: 真的是太有趣了，證明靈感往往來自最意想不到的地方。
segments.en: It's truly fascinating, proving inspiration often strikes from the most unexpected places.

segments.zh: 接下來，我們要轉換一下心情，關注一個比較沉重的議題。
segments.en: Next, we're shifting gears to focus on a more somber issue.

segments.zh: 你知道圈養的虎鯨，牠們的牙齒常常有嚴重磨損、斷裂，甚至是被鑽孔嗎？
segments.en: Did you know that captive orcas often have severely worn-down, broken, or even drilled teeth?

segments.zh: 這是因為牠們在壓力大又無聊的時候，會去啃咬水泥池壁和鋼製柵欄。
segments.en: This happens because, out of stress and boredom, they chew on concrete pool walls and steel gates.

segments.zh: 這真的是讓人聽了很心疼，也反映出圈養環境對牠們造成的巨大傷害。
segments.en: This is truly heartbreaking and highlights the immense harm caused by captive environments.

segments.zh: Reddit上很多網友都表示很難過，認為虎鯨不該被關在水族箱裡。
segments.en: Many Redditors expressed sadness, believing orcas shouldn't be kept in tanks.

segments.zh: 有人說：「這就是為什麼我們應該停止去海洋世界這種地方。」
segments.en: One user stated, "This is exactly why we should stop visiting places like SeaWorld."

segments.zh: 這些討論提醒我們，要更重視動物的福利與牠們的自然棲息地。
segments.en: These discussions remind us to prioritize animal welfare and their natural habitats.

segments.zh: 希望未來有更多虎鯨能回到廣闊的海洋，自由自在地生活。
segments.en: Hopefully, more orcas can return to the vast ocean and live freely in the future.

segments.zh: 最後，我們要來談談一個跟網路安全有關的警訊。
segments.en: Finally, let's discuss a crucial warning related to online security.

segments.zh: 美國聯邦調查局最新報告指出，北韓駭客用假視訊電話詐騙了四億美元。
segments.en: The FBI's latest report reveals North Korean hackers scammed four hundred million dollars using fake video calls.

segments.zh: 這些駭客利用所謂的「變臉竊賊」手法，讓九百多名受害者上當。
segments.en: These hackers used a "FaceStealer" scheme, tricking over nine hundred victims.

segments.zh: 他們會假冒成不同身份，引誘受害者加入視訊通話，然後竊取加密貨幣。
segments.en: They impersonate various identities, luring victims into video calls, then stealing cryptocurrency.

segments.zh: 這類詐騙手法越來越高明，很難靠肉眼辨識真偽。
segments.en: These scams are getting increasingly sophisticated, making them hard to identify visually.

segments.zh: 所以，在網路上遇到任何可疑的連結或通話請求，千萬要多方查證。
segments.en: So, always double-check any suspicious links or call requests online.

segments.zh: 保護好自己的數位資產，才不會落入詐騙集團的陷阱喔。
segments.en: Protect your digital assets to avoid falling into scammers' traps.

segments.zh: 今天的節目就到這裡告一段落，希望大家聽得開心也學到新東西。
segments.en: That's all for today's episode; I hope you enjoyed it and learned something new.

segments.zh: 感謝收聽，別忘了訂閱我們的頻道，下週同一時間再見囉！
segments.en: Thanks for tuning in, don't forget to subscribe to our channel, and see you next week!
